meta.nutritionDisclaimer: Nutrition is a loose per-serving estimate. Actual values depend on portions, brands, sauces, and add-ins.

items.name: Bibimbap bowls
items.summary: A composed rice bowl with several vegetables, protein, kimchi, and gochujang.

nutrition.notes: Higher with more rice or oil; add tofu, egg, or edamame for more protein.

items.name: Everyday tofu bowl
items.summary: Tofu, rice, vegetables, and a chosen sauce; the main flexible weeknight template.

nutrition.notes: Peanut sauce and larger rice portions move this toward the upper end.

items.name: Japanese curry
items.summary: Mild, thick curry with vegetables and rice; useful as an occasional comfort meal.

nutrition.notes: Protein varies most with tofu or chicken.

items.name: Fried rice
items.summary: A flexible use-up meal built around leftover rice, vegetables, and protein.

nutrition.notes: Kimchi fried rice is a built-in variation.

items.name: Tikka masala / butter chicken-style curry
items.summary: Tomato-rich Indian curry with cauliflower and either tofu or chicken.

nutrition.notes: Cream and butter raise calories; tofu or chicken keeps protein substantial.

items.name: Korma
items.summary: Creamy, aromatic curry with cauliflower and flexible protein.

nutrition.notes: Nuts, cream, and coconut milk increase the upper range.

items.name: Red lentil coconut curry
items.summary: A pantry-friendly, high-fiber curry with lentils, coconut milk, and vegetables.

nutrition.notes: Rice and full-fat coconut milk move calories upward.

items.name: Cowboy caviar
items.summary: A cold bean, corn, and vegetable mixture eaten plain or served with chips, tortillas, rice, or greens.

nutrition.serving: 1 meal-size portion, depending on serving style
nutrition.notes: Chips, tortillas, avocado, and cottage cheese create most of the range.

items.name: Loaded nachos
items.summary: Nachos with beans, spinach, vegetables, salsa, sour cream, and other chosen toppings.

nutrition.notes: Beans, vegetables, cheese, sour cream, and portion size create most of the range.

items.name: Zucchini pancakes
items.summary: Savory zucchini pancakes with sour cream or yogurt.

nutrition.notes: Oil absorption and topping amount affect calories substantially.

items.name: Vegetarian shepherd's pie
items.summary: Savory lentil, mushroom, and vegetable filling topped with mashed potatoes.

nutrition.notes: Butter, cheese, and portion size drive the upper end.

items.name: Vegetable pot pie
items.summary: Creamy vegetable filling under puff pastry, pie crust, or biscuits.

nutrition.notes: Pastry and protein choice create most of the range.

items.name: Enchiladas
items.summary: An occasional reminder meal for when a baked, saucy tortilla dish sounds good.

nutrition.notes: Cheese, tortilla size, and filling determine most of the range.

items.name: White bean kale stew
items.summary: A favorite hearty white bean stew with greens and herbs.

nutrition.notes: Bread, cheese, and oil raise calories.

items.name: Lentil soup
items.summary: A flexible everyday lentil soup: Mediterranean, tomato, lemon, or spinach.

nutrition.notes: Bread and oil account for much of the range.

items.name: Black bean soup
items.summary: Smoky or Southwest-style, blended or chunky.

nutrition.notes: Toppings create most of the upper range.

items.name: Split pea soup
items.summary: A mostly pantry-based, thick, comforting soup.

nutrition.notes: Bread and added fat raise calories.

items.name: Kimchi stew
items.summary: Kimchi, tofu, mushrooms, and broth, usually with rice on the side.

nutrition.notes: Rice and tofu amount create most of the range.

items.name: Coconut curry soup
items.summary: A flexible soup with coconut milk, curry paste, tofu, vegetables, and optional rice noodles.

nutrition.notes: Noodles and full-fat coconut milk increase calories.

items.name: Minestrone
items.summary: A vegetable-heavy clean-out-the-fridge soup with beans and pasta.

nutrition.notes: Pasta, cheese, and bread raise calories.

items.name: Tomato soup
items.summary: Simple tomato soup, especially good with grilled cheese or sourdough.

nutrition.notes: The wide range accounts for grilled cheese or a substantial bread side.

items.name: Miso soup
items.summary: A quick side or light meal with tofu, seaweed, and optional noodles.

nutrition.notes: Noodles and tofu turn this from a side into a light meal.

items.name: Flexible vegetable soup
items.summary: A general use-up soup for whatever vegetables are available.

nutrition.notes: Beans, lentils, pasta, and bread determine whether this is light or substantial.

items.name: Broccoli cheddar soup
items.summary: A richer occasional comfort soup.

nutrition.notes: Cheese, cream, and bread create most of the range.

items.name: Potato leek soup
items.summary: An occasional smooth comfort soup despite potatoes not being a frequent choice.

nutrition.notes: Cream, butter, and bread raise calories.

items.name: Fairlife protein shakes
items.stockRule: Keep 4 total: 2 at home and 2 at work.

nutrition.notes: Depends on product line.

items.name: Generate a grazing plate
items.summary: Choose 1–2 proteins, 1 crunch, 1 acidic item, 1 fruit or vegetable, and an optional extra.

nutrition.notes: The generator favors balance, but portions remain flexible.

items.name: Portable work snacks
items.summary: Quick items that can go in a bag or office fridge.

nutrition.notes: Choose a protein-forward option when the snack needs to carry a meal gap.

items.name: Cottage cheese snack
items.summary: Cottage cheese with chili crunch and honey.

nutrition.notes: Honey and chili crunch affect the upper end.

items.name: Yogurt dessert
items.summary: Yogurt with chia seeds and either frozen fruit or banana.

nutrition.notes: Fruit amount and yogurt type create most of the range.

items.name: Fruit dessert
items.summary: Fresh berries, frozen grapes, fruit salad, or baked fruit.

nutrition.notes: Greek yogurt raises protein.

items.name: Apple crisp or berry crumble
items.summary: A warm occasional dessert.

nutrition.notes: Topping size and ice cream create most of the range.

items.name: Sweet treat on hand
items.summary: Dark chocolate, cookies, or ice cream when that is what sounds good.
